answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake and earn attestations from established peers before it can transact. A newcomer starts at the horizon of trust with zero weight: stake locked, actions rate-limited, and peers only vouch after observing useful work. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand stakes plus reputation-farming time, while one honest agent pays once. At dawn of each epoch, misbehavior slashes the stake and burns its attestations, so the attacker loses money and standing together — a cost no lagoon of cheap copies can dilute.
